examples.question_text:
Convert:
(a) $17.6$ L/h to mL/h
(b) $263$ c/L to dollars per litre.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{17.6\text{ L}}{1\text{ h}}=\frac{17.6\times1000\text{ mL}}{1\text{ h}}=17\,600\text{ mL/h}$.
(b) $\frac{263\text{ c}}{1\text{ L}}=\frac{\$(263\div100)}{1\text{ L}}=\$2.63\text{/L}$.
Only the numerator units change.

examples.question_text:
Convert:
(a) $\$19$/kg to dollars per gram
(b) $13$ m/s to metres per hour.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{\$19}{1\text{ kg}}=\frac{\$19}{1000\text{ g}}=\$0.019\text{/g}$.
(b) $\frac{13\text{ m}}{1\text{ s}}=\frac{13\text{ m}}{(1\div3600)\text{ h}}=46\,800\text{ m/h}$.
A smaller denominator unit gives less per unit; a longer time unit gives more per unit.

examples.question_text: Convert $47$ L/h to mL/s, correct to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Convert both quantities separately:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{47\text{ L}}{1\text{ h}}\\&=\frac{47\times1000\text{ mL}}{3600\text{ s}}\\&=\frac{47\,000\text{ mL}}{3600\text{ s}}\\&\approx13.06\text{ mL/s}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Convert:
(a) $7.3$ m/s to km/h
(b) $41.4$ km/h to m/s.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{7.3\text{ m}}{1\text{ s}}=\frac{0.0073\text{ km}}{(1\div3600)\text{ h}}=26.28\text{ km/h}$.
(b) $\frac{41.4\text{ km}}{1\text{ h}}=\frac{41\,400\text{ m}}{3600\text{ s}}=11.5\text{ m/s}$.
Keep each conversion with its own quantity.

examples.question_text: A crop yield is $23$ t/ha. Convert it to kg/m$^2$.
examples.solution_text:
$1$ t $=1000$ kg and $1$ ha $=10\,000$ m$^2$.
$\frac{23\text{ t}}{1\text{ ha}}=\frac{23\,000\text{ kg}}{10\,000\text{ m}^2}=2.3\text{ kg/m}^2$
Use the area conversion factor, not a length conversion factor.

examples.question_text: A machine dispenses $9.7$ kg/day. Convert to g/min, correct to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
$1$ day $=24\times60=1440$ min.
$\frac{9.7\text{ kg}}{1\text{ day}}=\frac{9700\text{ g}}{1440\text{ min}}\approx6.74\text{ g/min}$
Convert the whole day to minutes before dividing.
